title: Towards Resilient Transportation: A Conditional Transformer for Accident-Informed Traffic Forecasting

problem.claim: Traffic prediction remains a key challenge in spatio-temporal data mining.

gap.claim: Existing models often overlook the influence of external factors such as traffic accidents and regulations because of limited data integration.

contributions.claim: The work presents two enriched traffic datasets from Tokyo and California that incorporate traffic accident and regulation data.
The work proposes ConFormer, a conditional transformer framework integrating graph propagation with a guided normalization layer.
The framework dynamically adjusts spatial and temporal node relationships based on historical patterns.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe ConFormer as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: ConFormer reportedly surpasses STAEFormer in predictive performance and efficiency, with lower computational costs and reduced parameter demands.
Extensive evaluations reportedly show that ConFormer consistently outperforms mainstream spatio-temporal baselines across multiple metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Traffic prediction is a persistent challenge, and external factors such as accidents and regulations complicate accurate forecasting.
The authors introduce enriched Tokyo and California traffic datasets containing accident and regulation data.
They propose ConFormer, which combines graph propagation and guided normalization to dynamically adjust spatial and temporal relationships.
The authors report improved predictive performance and efficiency relative to STAEFormer and other spatio-temporal baselines.
Code is reported as released in a public GitHub repository.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, time ranges, preprocessing, or train-validation-test splits.
The abstract does not provide metric values, statistical significance, or detailed comparison conditions.
The abstract does not describe the guided normalization layer or graph propagation mechanism in detail.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility of the reported results.
